description:
You are a computational immunologist at a vaccine research institute. Your team is developing a universal influenza vaccine targeting conserved epitope regions of the hemagglutinin (HA) protein. You have been given protein sequences of the HA1 subunit from 12 influenza A virus strains spanning different subtypes and years, located at ~/UGENE_Data/vaccine/influenza_HA_strains.fasta.

Perform the following multi-step analysis in UGENE:

1. Open the FASTA file containing 12 HA protein sequences and load them as an alignment.

2. Perform a multiple sequence alignment using MAFFT (not MUSCLE or ClustalW — MAFFT's L-INS-i strategy is standard for divergent viral protein alignments). If MAFFT is not available, use the best available algorithm.

3. After alignment, use UGENE's alignment statistics or conservation analysis features to identify regions of high conservation (>80% identity across all strains). These represent potential cross-reactive epitope targets.

4. For each highly conserved region of at least 9 consecutive amino acids (the minimum T-cell epitope length), create a new annotation:
   - Annotation name: 'conserved_epitope'
   - Group: 'vaccine_targets'
   - Include a /note qualifier describing the conservation level

5. Generate and export the consensus sequence from the alignment. Save it as ~/UGENE_Data/vaccine/results/HA_consensus.fasta

6. Save the annotated alignment as ~/UGENE_Data/vaccine/results/HA_alignment_annotated.aln (ClustalW format)

7. Export the alignment also in Stockholm format as ~/UGENE_Data/vaccine/results/HA_alignment.sto

8. Create a vaccine target report at ~/UGENE_Data/vaccine/results/epitope_report.txt listing:
   - Each conserved epitope region (position range and consensus sequence)
   - The conservation percentage for each epitope
   - A ranking of the top 3 epitope candidates by conservation score
   - The total number of conserved epitopes identified

metadata.data_source: NCBI Protein: 12 real HA sequences - AAD17229.1/ABD77675.1 (H1N1 1918), ACP41105.1 (H1N1 2009), ABQ44486.1 (H3N2 1968), AAT73274.1 (H5N1 2004), AGJ51966.1 (H7N9 2013), AAA43178.1 (H2N2 1957), plus seasonal and recent H1N1/H3N2/H5N1/H9N2 strains spanning 1918-2023
